findings.detail:
GOO CORRECTION — CLEAR (honest + buildable + soundly gated). Every load-bearing premise verified at the spec/source level: (1) morph-bridge.css is exactly 159L, merge-ONLY (two plates converge on one center via `filter: url(#…)` feGaussianBlur+feColorMatrix threshold, deterministic on --dock-morph-t — morph-bridge.css:1-90), so "fission is 1→N divergence, a NEW topology not a parameterization" is honest; the "drop zero-new-engine, it adds one orchestrator + one bridge recipe" framing is correct. (3) The SVG-clips-backdrop-filter WebKit constraint is REAL + spec-confirmed: Filter Effects L2 (drafts.csswg.org/filter-effects-2) says a filtered ancestor forms a Backdrop Root — "Allowing the Backdrop Root to read back content above a filtered element necessitates breaking the atomicity of the filter, with undefined results" — so the goo ancestor (filter:url()) and glass descendant (backdrop-filter) genuinely cannot coexist in WebKit; the "goo OR glass per-frame, resolved per-frame (goo during the neck, glass at rest)" constraint is the correct honest disposition. (4) The manual-real-Safari-26-Metal capture is a SOUND gate, NOT a dodge: the existing 4×-throttle perf gates (proof:morph-showcase, proof:dock-morph-insitu:167-176) already record the throttle p50 as a DELTA ARTEFACT ("dev-box truth"), NOT a born-RED auto-gate — and that 4× throttle is CDP/Chromium-only; the webkit Playwright project (tests-visual/playwright.config.ts:117, devices["Desktop Safari"], testMatch=safari-webgl+aurora-swraster) carries NO CDP throttle, confirming "the webkit project has none." So relaxing framesOver==0 to a measured p50 from a MANUAL real-Safari-26 capture mirrors the existing DELTA-recorded-perf precedent exactly. BLOCKED-ON BE.W-VIZ-PARITY-METAL is the honest dependency (proof-gpu-substrate-single.mjs:210-219 records the structural proxy on disk but the binding real-Metal capture rides forward — same posture).

SQUIRCLE-COVERAGE — CRITICAL paint-realizability defect (the mechanism cannot deliver its stated Safari paint). WAVE-LIST.md:67 says "corner-shape: superellipse coupling on card/chip/dock-control behind an @supports floor, so the iOS-27 superellipse silhouette reads on SAFARI." This is internally contradictory and false-as-written. (a) corner-shape:superellipse is Chromium-ONLY (Chrome 139+); Safari/Firefox "drop the property at parse time" and fall back to ordinary rounded corners (web-confirmed, MDN/caniuse/smashing 2026). (b) An `@supports (corner-shape: superellipse(2))` floor is EXACTLY the mechanism that keeps Safari rounded — Safari never enters the block. (c) This is already the HEAD state: src/styles/glass/squircle.css:33-34 literally states "Chrome 139+, no FF/Safari 2026 … the squircle is the better tier, NOT a degraded fallback" — so the @supports-corner-shape path leaves Safari rounded BY DESIGN today. The wave as written re-asserts the existing Chromium-only behavior while CLAIMING it reads on Safari. To actually PAINT the iOS-27 squircle silhouette on Safari (the wave's whole "the single most-visible iOS-27 shape cue" rationale) the wave needs a clip-path/shape() or SVG-clip mechanism (the web-confirmed Safari workaround; shape() "now supported on all major browsers"), with corner-shape as the Chromium progressive enhancement. The current mechanism is NOT Safari-verifiable in the claimed direction — a Safari π capture would show rounded corners, refuting the wave's own gate intent.

LENS-SAFARI — MAJOR under-spec (the real-displace path is buildable but the architecture is unstated). The correction is correct that proof:lensing is property-only (proof-lensing.mjs L1-L6 all check tokens/data-URI structure; lensing.spec.ts:72-90 is getComputedStyle+screenshot-only, ZERO getImageData rim-vs-interior readback) — so "the floor π must do a real pixel rim-vs-interior getImageData readback" is WARRANTED. Without that, the Safari "refraction" floor is a real-displace of nothing-behind. The pixel-readback gate is right; the capture mechanism needs one more design pass to be buildable-as-stated.

OTHER VISUAL WAVES — paint-capturable + Safari-verifiable + G7-revokable, none source-greenable: AMBIENT-TINT buildable (useGlassBackdropLuminance.ts already does drawImage+getImageData:237-248 + elementsFromPoint:284 — dominant-hue extension rides the existing substrate). SHEET-TRANSLUCENT capturable (--glass-opacity-dialog 0.68 / overlay 0.95 exist at glass.css:181/58; the new sheet ~0.74 between them is a real composited-fill delta). TINTED-CHIP/--glass-fill-tint verified ABSENT (net-new, distinct from shipped rim --glass-accent in cards.css/material.css). findings.detail:
=== (1) THE PER-CONTEXT goo-SIGNATURE — one --dock-split-t + a per-context DIRECTION-VECTOR + TIMING descriptor ===

SUBSTRATE: the fission driver mints `--dock-split-t` as the EXACT twin of `--dock-morph-t` (dockMorphContext.ts:275 writes the morph scalar to the root once/frame off ONE SpringProgress on DOCK_SPRING; the fission orchestrator clones that loop for a 0→1 detach scalar). Each surviving control becomes a fission PIECE registered like a MorphTarget (the `Set<MorphTarget>` pattern, dockMorphContext.ts:157), but instead of a from/to SIZE span it carries a per-piece DIRECTION-VECTOR + a context PROFILE. Reference-grounded against THREE distinct iOS-27 split signatures observed in /tmp/ios27-ref:

  • SEARCH = RADIAL BURST (f_034 is the COUNTER-case — search/menu actually peels; the radial is the search-FIELD-open case the betters-bar names). The pieces detach along the NORMALIZED RADIAL from the dock centroid: each piece's `--split-dx/--split-dy` = `(cx_i − cx_dock, cy_i − cy_dock)` unit-scaled, so controls fly outward like a bloom. The neck NECKS LATE (the goo holds until ~t=0.55 then snaps — a tense radial pop). TIMING: per-piece `animation-delay`-equivalent is `--split-stagger * radialRank(i)` (innermost-first), so the burst reads as an outward ripple not a simultaneous scatter.

  • MEDIA = LATERAL PEEL (f_034: the menu sheet PEELS DOWN off the toolbar pill with a visible triangular neck-nub at the sheet crown — the menu BUDS off the pill laterally/downward). The now-playing center piece STAYS (the f_021/f_055 translucent pill is the anchor); the flanking transport controls peel along the dock's CROSS axis (a horizontal dock peels block-ward, a vertical peels inline-ward — the `dimOf(axis)` idiom, dockMorphContext.ts:480 `morphAxisProp`). `--split-dx/--split-dy` = the fixed cross-axis unit, magnitude `--dock-rail-extend-length` (the stack-rail.css:37 gutter token — REUSED, the pieces peel into the SAME gutter the stack fans into). The neck is a LONG tapering tail (the f_034 nub), so `--split-neck-hold` is HIGH (the goo bridge survives the whole peel). TIMING: sequential outside-in (`--split-stagger * lateralRank(i)`).

  • NAV = INWARD MERGE (the reverse — nav controls MERGE toward the centroid then the dock re-forms as a bar). This is the morph-bridge.css merge-to-ONE (the 2-plate neck-to-center, morph-bridge.css:101-149) GENERALIZED to N pieces collapsing inward. `--split-dx/--split-dy` = the NEGATIVE radial (inward), and the scalar runs the bridge BACKWARD (`fission-bridge.css` is bidirectional by the same scalar — the re-merge the pass-3 list names). The neck SWELLS at the merge (`--stretch` peaks at the coalescence frame via useLiquidFlex, useLiquidFlex.ts:180 tanh law on the |Δt| derivative).

THE DESCRIPTOR (the ONE map the orchestrator reads): `DockSplitSignature = { context: "search"|"media"|"nav"; vector: "radial"|"lateral"|"inward-merge"; neckHold: number; staggerRank: (i, pieces) => number; squishPeak: "late"|"long"|"coalesce" }`. The per-context choreography is DATA, not three code paths — `useDockFission` reads the signature, computes each piece's `--split-dx/--split-dy/--i` off it, and the ONE fission-bridge.css recipe paints whatever vector the pieces carry. This is the df-topology zero-new-engine done HONESTLY: one new orchestrator (the fission driver) + one new recipe (fission-bridge.css generalizing morph-bridge.css from fixed-2-plate to N-piece-off-a-vector), per pass-3.

  COMPOSITOR-SAFETY: each piece's detach is `transform: translate(calc(var(--split-dx)*var(--dock-split-t)), …)` + the clip-path-inset neck (the shape.css:80-97 clip lerp pattern, already proven compositor-only on `--dock-morph-t`). ZERO layout property. PRM: the fission orchestrator mirrors dockMorphContext.ts:392 — a `prefersReducedMotion()` branch seats every piece at its `to` synchronously via nextTick (the seatTargetSync precedent), the goo bridge `--dock-bridge-opacity: 0` (morph-bridge.css:154), so the split is an instant cut, no neck, no scatter.

=== (2) THE POINTER-REACTIVE SEAM-TENSION FLOOR (f_021 — the neck visibly RESISTS the pull) ===

THE READ: in iOS the goo neck between a detaching piece and the dock body STRETCHES toward the pointer and visibly RESISTS — it thins as you pull, snaps back if you release short. The naive implementation (live clip-path-inset re-rasterize per pointermove) is the pass-3 Q285 perf-risk (the magnetic-tendril live-rerasterize). The COMPOSITOR-SAFE design:

  • usePointerVelocityField is the reader (usePointerVelocityField.ts) — but its `tick(delta)` is a PUSH-API needing a host frame loop (usePointerVelocityField.ts:222, the no-own-rAF discipline). The fission driver ALREADY owns a SpringProgress.play() rAF loop (the `--dock-split-t` writer); it calls `field.tick(delta)` from INSIDE that callback (the one-loop discipline, mirroring the viz `onFrame` pattern at usePointerVelocityField.ts:141-148). NO second rAF. The field reads `position`/`velocity`/`burst` in normalized-dock space (the pointer over the dock host, onPointerMove at usePointerVelocityField.ts:199).

  • THE TENSION is a SCALAR, not a re-rasterize. The neck's `clip-path: inset()` already interpolates on a var (shape.css:80, morph-bridge.css:118). We add ONE coupled tension term: `--seam-tension` = `clamp(0, field.velocity·k, --seam-tension-cap)` written ONCE per frame onto the dock scope (the SAME single-property-write the driver already does, dockMorphContext.ts:278). The neck-inset reads `inset(calc(--seam-neck − --seam-tension·--seam-give) … round 999px)` — so a fast pull THINS the neck (the resist read) via the EXISTING clip-path channel, no new layer, no re-rasterize (the browser re-interpolates the one inset value the compositor already animates). The "resist" comes free: the inset is driven by `--dock-split-t` (the spring) MINUS `--seam-tension` (the pointer) — pull faster than the spring releases and the neck visibly stretches-then-snaps when you release (the spring re-bases from velocity, dockMorphContext.ts:255 inheritedVelocity, so the snap-back is the iOS interruptible contract already shipped).

  • THE CAP (anti-slop): `--seam-tension-cap` is LOW (≈0.12, the useLiquidFlex maxStretch ≈1.08 register, useLiquidFlex.ts:52 "kept LOW — never a taffy-pull"). The squish that swells the neck under tension rides useLiquidFlex's tanh law (useLiquidFlex.ts:185) — saturating, so a frantic pull caps, never taffy.

  • PERF (the f_021 risk killed structurally): NO per-frame clip-path RE-RASTERIZE — a clip-path inset is a compositor mask the browser interpolates without re-rasterizing the masked content (it's the same channel shape.css already animates on every dock morph, proof:no-layout-animation GREEN). The bridge filter (feGaussianBlur, morph-bridge.css:50-61) is `contain: layout paint` over a TIGHT box (morph-bridge.css:55-59), so even the goo region is bounded. The tension only moves the inset NUMBER, not the filter graph.

  • PRM-OFF: `field.tick(0)` freezes velocity to rest (usePointerVelocityField.ts:224 the tick(0) discipline), so `--seam-tension` resolves 0 → the neck is the pure spring inset, no pointer reactivity. The fission still functions (the spring seats), the resist is just off — vestibular-safe.

=== (3) THE RAIL+FISSION FUSION — the detached sub-dock ANCHORS to a rail facet, ONE engine ===

THE GAP: today the rail (DockStack, BC.W-DOCK-STACK-RAIL) and the fission split are two unrelated mechanisms. The betters-move: when the dock FISSIONS, a detached piece doesn't fly to a void — it lands ON a DockStack facet (the macOS hover-fan member). One engine, three reuses:

  • THE ANCHOR: DockStack renders in `GlassDock`'s `#rail` slot over the `.glass-dock-frame` non-clipping escape (DockStack.vue:13, stack-rail.css:6-14 — the box-INVIOLATE positioning context). The fission piece's `to`-target is a DockStack member's CLIENT rect (the f_055 tab-bar items are the landing seats). The fission orchestrator reads the member geometry the SAME way useDockOrientationMorph reads its size getters (useDockOrientationMorph.ts:46-48 `verticalSize/horizontalSize` as `() => number` live FLIP getters) — a `() => memberRect` getter per piece, so the detach interpolates `from` (the in-dock control) → `to` (the rail facet) off `--dock-split-t` via the ElementMorph+springTimingFunction FLIP (the useLiquidReveal substrate the pass-3 names, the SAME `ElementMorph(settledRect, triggerRect)` shape).

  • ONE SCALAR, ONE SPRING: the fission detach AND the rail facet's hover-fan share the dock's DOCK_SPRING clock (DockStack already speaks the iOS liquid clock via `--spring-dock`, stack-rail.css:192; the fission writes `--dock-split-t` off DOCK_SPRING). When a piece lands on a facet, the facet's `is-active` register (stack-rail.css:229) lights — the piece hands off (the useDockCtaReceive `onReceived` precedent, CLAUDE.md BB.B2: fly + reshape onto a foreign dock-control target, fade opacity 1→0, congest filter blur 0→4px, hand off). The fission piece IS a CTA-receive consumer pointed at a rail facet.

  • THE GOO CONNECTS THEM: the neck (fission-bridge.css) bridges the in-dock control to the rail facet so the piece reads as ONE liquid surface stretching from dock to facet (not a piece teleporting). The goo region `contain`-box (morph-bridge.css:55) sizes off the dock-edge-to-facet span (a new `--split-bridge-w/h` consumer var, the same shape the bridge already takes `--dock-bridge-h-w`, morph-bridge.css:55).

  • box-INVIOLATE PRESERVED: the rail lives in the gutter outside the dock clip (stack-rail.css:50-59 the `.glass-dock-frame[data-has-rail]` non-clipping context), and the fission piece detaching to it paints in that SAME non-clipping frame — so the dock box never grows (deltaW=deltaH=0, the DockStack.vue:8 discipline). The per-facet `--glass-accent` (the BE.W-DOCK-TINTED-CHIP per-facet accent-hue FLOOR, reading glass/rim.css:82 + material.css:137) tints both the facet AND the landing piece's congesting glass, so the piece arrives carrying the facet's hue (the f_009/f_018 ambient-tint read — the piece absorbs the target's color as it merges).

  • THE GATE: `proof:dock-rail-realize` extends `proof:dock-stack-rail` (the LIVE successor — `proof:rail3` is DELETED, removed at BC 0aa16913, per pass-3). The fusion clause asserts: the fission `to`-getter resolves a DockStack member rect, the detach rides DOCK_SPRING (no second spring), the hand-off fires the facet `is-active`, box stays INVIOLATE (deltaW=deltaH=0 across the detach).

findings.detail:
**(1) AMBIENT-HUE — extend useGlassBackdropLuminance to extract the dominant HUE.** The substrate is ready: useGlassBackdropLuminance.ts already runs a 32×32 downsample + getImageData (lines 196-265, SAMPLE_DOWNSAMPLE=32) and walks every pixel computing relLuminance. The hue extraction is a CHEAP rider over the SAME `data` Uint8ClampedArray loop (line 256-264) — no second canvas, no second pass. MECHANISM: in the existing per-pixel loop, accumulate a hue HISTOGRAM not just luminance — convert each composited-over-white sRGB triple to OKLCh (reuse the value.js cssToOklch/oklchToLinear leaf the aurora-swraster fallback already imports, NOT a hand-rolled conversion — proof:single-color-core fence), bin into 12 hue buckets weighted by chroma×alpha (low-chroma pixels contribute ~0 — a gray backdrop yields no dominant hue, the correct null). Pick the modal bucket, refine to its chroma-weighted circular-mean hue → write `--glass-ambient-hue` (a complete oklch() color at a FIXED sub-perceptual chroma/L, NOT the raw sampled chroma — the ambient bias is a HUE event, the plate must not absorb the backdrop's saturation). THE BIAS SEAM: a NEW opt-in token `--glass-ambient-strength` (default 0%, the no-op floor) biases `--glass-tint-source` toward `--glass-ambient-hue` via `color-mix(in oklab, var(--glass-tint-ink), var(--glass-ambient-hue) var(--glass-ambient-strength))` — this rides the EXACT existing tint cascade at ladder.css:154/213/275 (the self-engage re-point) with ZERO new compositing seam. CEILING: bounded ≤8% (sub-perceptual — f_009→f_010 shows the field warming TOWARD the album amber, not becoming it). Throttle inherits the ≤4Hz loop (line 173); PRM collapses to the single mount sample (line 360). The histogram is +~12 floats/sample, free. Verified ABSENT (`grep glass-ambient` → 0 hits). Wire-on default for the DOCK only (the H3 arm-a precedent at the dock's now-playing surface); demo-private barrel posture preserved. GATE proof:ambient-hue: A1 the histogram derived in the SAME loop (no 2nd pass), A2 the value.js color source (no hand-rolled rgb→oklch), A3 chroma-weighted (a gray backdrop → null hue, born-RED self-test with a flat-gray fixture), A4 the bias rides --glass-tint-source at ≤8% (no new compositing path), A5 PRM single-sample + the ≤4Hz floor. Binding π: a warm-amber backdrop vs a cool-teal backdrop resolve DISTINCT --glass-ambient-hue and the plate's getComputedStyle background shifts sub-perceptually toward each, both modes.

**(2) SQUIRCLE cross-engine — corner-shape:superellipse @supports floor + the Safari fallback.** ROOT FINDING: the iOS-27 squircle silhouette is encoded in TWO disjoint places, BOTH Chromium-only. (a) glass-refract.css's displacement map bakes the squircle PROFILE f(x)=⁴√(1−(1−x)⁴) (lines 14-17) but the whole filter is gated behind `@supports (backdrop-filter: url(#…))` which Safari NEVER enters (WebKit bug 245510, confirmed OPEN). (b) squircle.css:39 gates `corner-shape: superellipse(2)` behind `@supports (corner-shape: superellipse(2))` — Chrome 139+ only; Safari 26 does NOT ship corner-shape. So today Safari reads PLAIN border-radius on every surface — the single most-visible iOS-27 shape cue is exactly what Safari loses. THE BETTERS-MOVE: squircle.css already has the @supports floor pattern + the per-surface tokenized `var(--corner-shape-<surface>)` (lines 40-52); BE.W-SQUIRCLE-COVERAGE EXTENDS it two ways: (i) WIDEN the corner-shape coupling from the overlay-band-only set (dialog/sheet/panel/hero) to the card/chip/dock-control families AT/ABOVE the read threshold (the policy at lines 6-19 keeps small-radius pills round — correct; but the big card + the Maps facet-chip + the dock-control plate ARE above ~--radius-xl where the superellipse reads). The @supports floor means a non-supporting engine paints the SAME `border-radius` round contract (lines 61-65 precedent) — never a degraded fallback, the better-tier-or-round discipline. (ii) THE SAFARI-NATIVE PATH (the genuine cross-engine betters, folds into LENS-SAFARI): Safari supports `filter: url(#displace)` (the REGULAR filter property, feDisplacementMap IS WebKit-supported — distinct from backdrop-filter:url which is NOT) over a captured/duplicated backdrop layer; the SAME squircle displacement map already baked in glass-refract.css can drive a Safari-native edge-lens via a regular `filter` on a backdrop-clone layer. So Safari gets the squircle EDGE-LENSING (the real refraction), not just the corner SHAPE. CITE: the displacement map data-URI at glass-refract.css's --glass-refract-filter is reusable verbatim for the regular-filter path; only the host changes (a ::before backdrop-clone vs the backdrop-filter descendant). GATE proof:bloom-up: BU1 the 4 coupled channels (scale/opacity/blur/ambient-tint), BU2 the tint write is a custom-property NOT a background animation (the compositor-only self-test: a synthetic background-color write reds), BU3 the re-tint rides the destRef field not the source surface, BU4 PRM endpoint-snap, BU5 off-root-barrel /motion (the SCC-trap, useLiquidReveal precedent).

**(5) CLEAR-VARIANT — the now-playing pill permanent-translucent + MANDATORY scrim.** THE iOS CONTRACT (f_035/f_055/v2 f_009/f_018): the now-playing pill is PERMANENTLY translucent over a live media grid — the album covers bleed THROUGH it — but a dimming-scrim keeps the title legible (f_035 "The Sleeping Beauty" reads over the album grid; v2 f_009 "Daphnis Et Chloé" reads over the purple "Your Essentials" card). THE RISK (resolved): a translucent pill WITHOUT a coupled scrim reads as either opaque (if the plate is too dense) or illegible (if too clear).
